topic: Apollo 11 and the Journey to the Moon

text.content: During the 1960s, the United States and the Soviet Union were engaged in a fierce competition to explore outer space. Wanting to prove their technological superiority, the American government announced an incredibly ambitious goal. They promised to safely send human beings to the surface of the moon and bring them back before the end of the decade. This massive scientific effort required the hard work of thousands of engineers, mathematicians, and pilots.

To escape the gravity of the Earth, the engineers had to build the largest and most powerful machine ever created. Standing over 100 meters tall, it was filled with millions of liters of highly explosive rocket fuel. The massive machine successfully used to push the astronauts into the dark emptiness of space was known as the Saturn V rocket. Inside the tiny cabin at the very top of the rocket, three brave astronauts began their long journey.

After traveling through space for three days, the astronauts finally reached their destination. Two of the men climbed into a smaller landing craft and slowly flew down toward the rocky surface. The flat, dark area where the small spaceship finally landed safely is known as the Sea of Tranquility. When the heavy door opened, history was made. The man who first stepped onto the dusty surface and spoke those famous words was an American astronaut. His name was Neil Armstrong.

For the next two hours, the astronauts worked quickly outside their spaceship. Because there is no wind or rain on the moon, the footprints they left in the dust will likely remain there for millions of years. They collected heavy bags of rocks and dirt to bring back to the scientists on Earth. They also left behind a special mirror that scientists still use today to measure the exact distance between the Earth and the moon.

After finishing their important work, the astronauts fired their engine and flew back up to join their waiting friend in orbit. The return trip to Earth took another three days, ending with the spaceship safely splashing into the Pacific Ocean. The success of this mission proved that human beings could survive and travel beyond their home planet, forever changing how we view our place in the universe.

questions.prompt: All three of the astronauts climbed into the smaller landing craft and walked on the moon together.
questions.explanation: Paragraph C specifically states that 'Two of the men climbed into a smaller landing craft', meaning the third astronaut stayed behind.

questions.prompt: Because there is no wind or rain on the moon, the astronauts' footprints will likely remain there for millions of years.
questions.explanation: Paragraph D explicitly states: 'Because there is no wind or rain on the moon, the footprints they left in the dust will likely remain there for millions of years.'

questions.prompt: The special mirror left on the moon cost the American government two million dollars to build.
questions.explanation: Paragraph D mentions that a special mirror was left behind to measure distance, but it provides absolutely no information about how much money it cost to build.
